stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Folklorists have long observed that animal tricksters fill several distinct roles in West African oral storytelling. Some tricksters act as fools whose schemes collapse on them, while others serve as cultural heroes. ______ the spider Anansi often appears as a bringer of knowledge: in many tellings, he wins all the world's stories from the sky god and carries them down to people on earth.
explanation: The first sentences name a category with a plural noun: 'several distinct roles.' The sentence after the blank agrees with that claim and gives one member of the category, Anansi as a bringer of knowledge. One instance drawn from a larger group takes 'For example.'

A.why: You read the narrower sentence as a restatement. 'In other words' would mean the Anansi sentence repeats the claim about several roles in different terms. Instead, it adds new information: one specific trickster and one specific role.

C.why: You took the vivid detail about the sky god as a reversal. The Anansi sentence supports the claim that tricksters serve as cultural heroes and contradicts nothing, so a contrast word does not fit.

D.why: You treated the passage as a sequence of steps or a list reaching its last item. Nothing here is ordered in time, and the sentence gives an example instead of concluding a series.

subtype_name: General claim, then the detail (For example vs Specifically / In particular)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: For years, astronomers at a small mountaintop observatory struggled to capture clear images of faint, distant galaxies. In 2019, the observatory's staff made one upgrade to its main telescope that sharply improved those images. ______ they replaced the telescope's aging camera sensor with a new one able to detect nearly twice as much of the incoming light.
explanation: The second sentence mentions a single, unnamed action: 'one upgrade.' The sentence after the blank tells you exactly what that upgrade was. Nothing is being picked from a set. The same claim is being spelled out more precisely, so 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You saw a general claim followed by a detail and chose 'For example.' The passage says the staff made only one upgrade, so the sensor replacement is not one example among several. It is the upgrade itself, described in detail.

B.why: You treated the detail as a contradiction. Replacing the sensor is the upgrade that improved the images, so the sentence agrees with what came before and does not push against it.

D.why: 'Similarly' introduces a second, comparable thing. The sensor replacement is not a separate change resembling the upgrade. It is the same upgrade, named.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A 2021 study that followed 300 recreational runners through a full training season identified several habits that predicted injury. The researchers tracked each runner's mileage, footwear, sleep, and warm-up routine from week to week. ______ runners who raised their weekly distance by more than 30 percent at any point were nearly three times as likely as other runners to develop shin pain.
explanation: The passage names a category with a plural noun: 'several habits that predicted injury.' The sentence after the blank presents one of those habits, increasing mileage too fast, along with its effect. One member drawn from a larger group takes 'For instance.'

B.why: You treated the narrower sentence as a rephrasing. The mileage finding adds new information the earlier sentences never stated, such as the 30 percent threshold and the tripled risk of shin pain, so it is not a restatement.

C.why: 'Instead' signals that one option replaces another. The mileage finding doesn't replace anything. It is one of the habits the study identified.

D.why: You read the passage as a timeline. The final sentence reports a result of the study and isn't an event that came after the tracking, so a time-order word misstates the relationship.
